body:
HANDLES AND TRAPS (scheduler.py and test_scheduler.py read 6 Nov 2026, main 068c71a; B-39 has the proof and the numbers).

THE LINES. `Scheduler._claim` (scheduler.py:~270-307) selects `ORDER BY i.priority, i.created_at LIMIT 200`, keeps the rows of the best priority, and only then picks the person served longest ago (`turn`, line ~295). So the 200 oldest rows decide who can be served. Fair share has to be decided IN the query: for the best priority, rank people by when they were last served, take that person's oldest due item.

TRAP 1: the fairness memory is in RAM. `self._served` and `self._turn` (lines 104-105, 304-306) are lost at every restart, so after one the big importer is first again (all counters 0, ties by `created_at`). Derive "last served" from the database instead: the latest `updated_at` of a running, done or failed item per person through `work_item_person`. That also survives a second server process and needs no new column.

TRAP 2: priority stays first. The tests pin it: test_work_is_taken_by_priority_whatever_the_order_it_was_asked_in (78) and test_a_tap_on_a_song_being_kept_moves_it_to_the_front (90, `promote`). An item several people want is served on the turn of whoever waited longest (the existing rule): keep it.

TRAP 3: idle workers take the write lock. `_claim` opens `self._db.tx()` (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`) on every poll; the loop polls every second per worker (`_loop`, line ~381-391; background has 2 workers). Look with `db.read()` first and open the write transaction only when an item is due (the B-10 family; same rule as "no write lock for a plain read"). The interactive pool has no handler, so `kinds` is empty and it returns before the lock: do not start that worker until `prepare` exists (P1-04, B-66).

THE TEST THAT IS TOO SMALL: test_people_take_turns_so_a_big_import_cannot_starve_a_small_one (102-114) uses 5 + 2 items and asserts the small one is done within the first four. It passes under the 200-row window. Add the 2,000 + 20 case (the probe: `python -X utf8 docs/evidence/scripts/audit_probes.py fair-share`, whose last line must say the 20 run among the first ~40) and a restart in the middle (new `Scheduler` on the same database: the order must not reset).

DOCS: docs/04 section 10 rule 4 and docs/07 section 6 promise this; update their "built" wording only when the 2,000 + 20 test exists. Related and separate: the 12 s global pacer (B-42(b)) decides how many songs per hour, this decides whose.
